content: {"rule": "K-S2", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge assigns UNDERDETERMINED on a single verse (Luke 2:48-49) and reasons only from what that verse does or does not state, which is exactly what the rule governs.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4; Mary's phrase 'thy father' is immediately qualified by the child's reference to 'my Father's business.'", "rule_words": "That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side.", "room": "'never a ground for UNDERDETERMINED': reading one, the judge may weigh the verse's wording and still declare UNDERDETERMINED so long as it cites other rounds; reading two, the rule forbids resting an UNDERDETERMINED on what a single verse leaves unsettled, which this text does.", "why": "The verdict's stated basis is the internal qualification of one verse's wording rather than the chain links it elsewhere cites, so the single verse's failure to decide is made the ground of UNDERDETERMINED."}
